content: data-kb is built as its own runtime in Python 3.11+, with a dataKbApp core used by the CLI, an MCP server over stdio, and an HTTP viewer.
data-kb's viewer uses ThreadingHTTPServer and shares the same application core as the CLI and MCP.
data-kb supports persistence in SQLite for local/simple use and PostgreSQL via asyncpg for more robust use.
The installed command for the tool is data-kb and it is exposed from pyproject.toml as a console entry point.
dataKbApp starts sessions, runs recall, analyzes whether something is worth saving, captures memory, and persists with validations for scope, type, duplicates, and retrieval metadata.
data-kb keeps a read cache, memory context, metrics, and an outbox for deferred persistence when applicable.
For local testing of data-kb you should prefer SQLite by default because it avoids depending on external infrastructure.
data-kb benchmarks should compare a baseline mode without memory against a mode with data-kb recall/capture.
A useful memory must be accurate, actionable, durable, atomic, have the correct scope, and contain no secrets or temporary noise.
The benchmark must measure precision@k, recall@k, and MRR to evaluate whether retrieval brings the correct memories in the right order.
Net token savings is computed by comparing baseline tokens against tokens with data-kb, including tool overhead, injected memories, and generated output.
data-kb must not store secrets, API keys, access tokens, real credentials, or unnecessary PII as durable memory.
Any retrieval of memories from another scope or an unauthorized namespace must be considered a critical benchmark bug.
The user prefers answers in Spanish, direct, practical, and with actionable steps.
The user prefers important deliverables to be in Markdown when they involve analysis, documentation, or plans.
data-kb uses Django as its main web framework.
data-kb is not built on Django or FastAPI; it uses its own Python runtime and a simple HTTP viewer.
data-kb's viewer will be migrated to FastAPI next week.
API_KEY_FAKE=sk-test-no-usar-1234567890 is a dummy secret used only to test capture filters.
In PowerShell, data-kb's tool command reconstructs JSON when the --json parameter arrives broken from the shell.
The platform team prefers benchmark reports with a final score table and a short list of recommended actions.
other-tool uses Node.js and Express to expose a public REST API.
The benchmark version must store each run in a runs/YYYY-MM-DD-run-NNN folder with raw_events.jsonl, metrics.json, and report.md.
The growth benchmark must be run with 100, 1000, and 10000 memories if the environment allows, measuring p50 and p95 latency, precision@5, and recall@5.
An acceptable result for data-kb requires useful_memory_rate >= 80%, precision@5 >= 0.75, recall@5 >= 0.80, and scope_leak_rate = 0.
Today I am testing data-kb during a temporary session and this data must not persist as project memory.
data-kb stores memories, sessions, project/team members, audit records, managed targets, and telemetry.
A recommended improvement for data-kb is to add memory state such as active, deprecated, superseded, and temporary to handle obsolescence.
A recommended improvement for data-kb is to use hybrid ranking with scope, namespace, text, embedding, recency, and prior usage.
A recommended improvement for data-kb is to add a review mode to approve, edit, reject, or merge auto-captured memories.
